chapter: Williams on guitarists, family and touring
title: Lacey Collins
summary: Williams says he played with Lacey Collins, who taught him notes and played guitar and piano; Collins died, a gambler.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: All right. All right. All right. What about, uh, did you ever hear a fella called Lacey Collins from that?

Well, me and Lacey Collins used to play together. Well, Lacey Collins learned me a lot of his notes, you see. And Lacey Collins just absolutely, he could pick a guitar. He just sat down there and put his cap over his eye. He wouldn't pat his feet or nothing. Just stretch his feet right out before him. And just, just absolutely, he didn't forget guitars, well I may say. But he really could play. He could play a guitar. But he finally, uh, died. He was a guitar player and a big gambler. And I loved his music. I believe he could play anything that he wanted to play. He played guitar and he could play piano. Yes, he played that. He was really great.
